ProjectAmp2

Multi-project portfolio for the [&] Protocol ecosystem. Contains the protocol spec, reference implementations, portfolio company sites, and roughly 46 sub-repositories and **18 *.com / *.org directories** (counted 2026-09-19). It used to say "three active codebases"; that number described this tree in April.

Audited against the tree 2026-09-19. Every path, port and count below was checked by running the command or opening the file. What this pass found and fixed:

  • `WebHost.Systems/` no longer exists — renamed to locu.systems/. The bullet that described

the old name as deliberately retained is retracted in place, below.

  • `super/`, `computedriven/`, `TRVM/` and `WRL/` had no entry here at all, and the first two are

the two most active repositories in the tree.

  • Verified unchanged and correct: the box-and-box law totals (**109 kernel + 101 compose = 210

enforced, 3 declared-open**, re-derived by running both suites), all five T&R ports in .claude/launch.json, every docs/spec/ path named below, and that runefort.com/docs/spec/ still has no README.md.

The data layer — Supabase is ABANDONED; the replacement is studbook

Ruled by Travis 2026-07-30. This section used to teach the shared-Supabase route as current architecture, and did so for sixteen days after the decision. Do not restore it.

  • `studbook/docs/spec/README.md` is the spec. **R99 (Travis, 2026-09-28) opens ONE bounded implementation,

SB0**; the ruled text is row R99 of REVISION_REGISTER.md.

  • What SB0 is: experimental and non-confidential. One pedigree store; the first fixture is the gitec Phase A

lineage; the stud- namespace for studbook.record.v1.

  • What SB0 may build: canonical records, typed edges, verified closure, CAS head publication, and a

rebuildable SQLite projection that is never authoritative.

  • Still forbidden: confidential or user data, auth, networking, a query language, pager/WAL/B-tree,

replication, prolly trees.

  • Still unruled: §10.1, §10.2 and track-. Build nothing outside R99. Until 2026-09-28 this line said

"do not build from this yet"; R15 was narrowed, not lifted.

  • Why Supabase went (studbook §2): Postgres stores a row but not why the row is that row, and

nothing in the migration layer could refuse a row whose provenance did not check out — so the stack's central claim, that a divergence is refusable rather than silent, stopped at the database boundary. It was also a dependency the stack does not control.

  • `ampersand-supabase/` is archived, not failed. Its 40 migrations across 10 schemas

(counted in the tree 2026-08-15; this said "35 across 11", a number copied from a JSON example in workbench/docs/spec/README.md and never re-derived) still apply and the code against them still runs. The directory now carries a README.md saying it is archived — until 2026-08-15 nothing in it did, and its ARCHITECTURE.md still opens "Status: Implementation-ready". Nothing migrates off it until studbook can hold the same data with the same guarantees (studbook §9). fleet.* still serves KILN and FleetPrompt today; kag.* has been orphaned since the BendScript pivot.

  • The blocker is one unruled question — studbook §10.2, where confidentiality comes from.

Content addressing is hostile to access control: if the key is the hash of the content, knowing the content is knowing the key. Until it is answered studbook cannot hold anything with a user in it, so it is not yet the replacement for what locu.systems and FleetPrompt use Supabase Auth and RLS for.

  • Products that never used Supabase: Graphonomous (embedded SQLite), Deliberatic (in-memory),

OpenSentience (ETS).

Read before doing data-layer work: studbook/docs/spec/README.md, then PUBLISH_PATH.md (the first named consumer) and STACK_HUB.md (compute/storage split and the provider question).

Standing direction, as of 2026-08-15

  • Compute moves into the ComputeDriven OS (T&R), run in a VM locally or in the cloud. The Fly.io

apps become storage or nothing — and R96 (2026-09-19) settles it as NOTHING: every Fly machine is torn down and Fly leaves the estate entirely. The cloud is `locu.systems` and ComputeDriven only; everything else runs on Travis's own machine. Nothing has been torn down yet, graphonomous-mcp goes last (fleetprompt.com and PRISM both call it), and box-and-box-mcp goes first because it is orphaned dead code. Identity is WorkOS AuthKit (R95), not Keycloak — which is what removed Fly's last reason to exist. T&R cannot run on Fly — Firecracker is Linux-guest only and nested virtualisation is refused, so a cloud VM needs a provider that boots custom images.

  • T&R is an operating system: the backup is the user's machine, 10 GB to 10 TB. Do not re-scope

it to "the shell's graph" — that error has already been made once and is recorded in WORLD_SIZE.md §11.

  • Cloudflare for everything; Fly keeps only Keycloak — ruled 2026-08-15 (R4).

STACK_HUB.md §0.6 is the reasoning; REVISION_REGISTER.md is the ruling. CORRECTED 2026-08-21 — this line said "recommended over Fly and not yet ruled" and was stale for six days, in the file that is prepended to every session in this tree. It also named D1, which R7 has since removed from the architecture: Pigsty owns application state, and D1 holds none.

  • Cloud v1 has no server-hosted BEAM (R7). The control plane is Cloudflare Workers reaching

Pigsty over Hyperdrive → Workers VPC → Cloudflare Tunnel. Super is Elixir/OTP on the user's machine — that is not a reason for the cloud to be. See CLOUD_V1.md.

  • "World" means three different sizes and each has its own name (R11) — WORLD is the machine

(10 GB–10 TB), WORLD VERSION is a manifest root in R2, WRL GRAPH is the small semantic layer inside it. CLOUD_V1.md §2 is the vocabulary; conflating them is the WORLD_SIZE.md §11 error.

  • `REVISION_REGISTER.md` lists what still contradicts these. Check it before trusting an older

planning doc.

Build commands

graphonomous (Elixir)

cd graphonomous
mix deps.get
mix compile --warnings-as-errors
mix test

locu.systems (Node.js)

cd locu.systems
npm install
npm run dev          # Vite dev server
npm run typecheck
npm run lint

AmpersandBoxDesign (Elixir reference impl)

cd AmpersandBoxDesign/reference/elixir/ampersand_core
mix deps.get
mix escript.build
./ampersand validate ../../../examples/infra-operator.ampersand.json

Conventions

  • Elixir code uses mix format style

  • TypeScript uses ESLint + Prettier

  • Commits should be clear and focused (see AmpersandBoxDesign/CONTRIBUTING.md)

  • Do not commit secrets, API keys, or credentials

  • EXLA is included in graphonomous deps for fast neural embeddings (requires LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/cuda/lib64; falls back gracefully)

  • graphonomous MCP uses a vendored anubis_mcp patch in vendor/anubis_mcp

Browser testing (ALL ProjectAmp2 projects)

Default browser automation tool: `agent-browser` (the anthropic-skills:agent-browser skill / agent-browser CLI).

This applies repo-wide — super/, graphonomous/, locu.systems/, AmpersandBoxDesign/, bendscript.com/, PRISM/, PULSE/, and every *.com/ / *.org/ marketing site.

Use agent-browser for:

  • Navigating pages, filling forms, clicking, taking screenshots

  • Scraping / extracting data from rendered pages

  • Testing web apps, login flows, SPAs

  • Exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts

  • Automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, etc.)

  • Cloud browser providers (Vercel Sandbox microVMs, AWS Bedrock AgentCore)

Prefer agent-browser over:

  • mcp__Claude_in_Chrome__* (Claude in Chrome MCP)

  • mcp__plugin_chrome-devtools-mcp_chrome-devtools__* (chrome-devtools MCP)

  • mcp__Claude_Preview__* for browser-level testing (preview_* is still fine for dev-server management and HMR; use agent-browser once a server is running and you want real browser interaction)

  • Any ad-hoc Playwright / Puppeteer / Selenium scripts

Bootstrap pattern for any session doing browser work:

agent-browser skills get core --full    # load the core skill
agent-browser open <url>                # navigate
agent-browser snapshot                  # a11y-tree snapshot (preferred over screenshot for assertions)
agent-browser screenshot                # visual proof when sharing with the user

Exception: if a task is narrowly about Chrome DevTools-specific features (Lighthouse audits, performance traces, heap snapshots), the chrome-devtools MCP may be used — but default to agent-browser for everything else.

A graphical VM is NOT browser work — use QEMU directly

For anything running inside a PARKVPS guest (the T&R distro, RRABBIT on the road, a greeter, a boot menu), do not reach for a browser. QEMU hands over both directions:

python3 PARKVPS/vpsd/vps.py screenshot tr4 /tmp/g.ppm   # the framebuffer
magick /tmp/g.ppm /tmp/g.png                            # no python PIL on this box
python3 PARKVPS/vpsd/vps.py type tr4 driver @tab driver @ret

This reaches what ssh cannot see at all — the display manager before anyone has logged in, a session that failed to start, an X server on the wrong VT. ssh tells you what a shell says is true; screenshot shows you the screen.

The T&R / RRABBIT / RAVIO local stack

These four run together and are easy to confuse. All are in the root .claude/launch.json; `RRABBIT/docs/RUNBOOK.md` is the authoritative runbook (port map, the probes that settle arguments, the traps).

  • 8911 npm run m0 — RRABBIT from source (vite, HMR)

  • 8912 npm run proxy — compositor-proxy, native applications

  • 8913 RRABBIT/bridge.py — the built shell + tubes; this is what the distro ships

  • 8905 PARKVPS/vpsd/api.py — the machines; /desktop/<name> shows a guest's screen

  • 8890 RAVIO/bridge.py — the sky road; its MACHINES rail (gear P) frames 8905

Two traps that have each cost a session: tools/proxy.sh defaults --allow-origin to 8911, so testing the built shell on 8913 needs RRABBIT_ALLOW_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:8913 or the launch fails with a CORS error that reads like the proxy being down; and restart the proxy between page reloads, because a proxy session outlives the page and a reload silently joins a session whose client is gone.

Graphonomous — v1 is LEGACY; the session memory loop is OFF

Ruled by Travis 2026-09-27. This section used to be "Graphonomous session policy (ALL ProjectAmp2 sessions)" and told every session to adopt a "Graphonomous-first memory loop" through the Graphonomous MCP (retrieve → route → act → learn → consolidate). Do not restore it, and do not call mcp__plugin_graphonomous_graphonomous__* tools.

  • Why: the v1 engine (v0.4.3) deleted everything it stored. Its consolidator runs every 5 minutes,

decays every node's confidence by 2 % and hard-deletes below 0.1, so a node stored at 0.5 is gone in about 7 hours; ~/.graphonomous/knowledge.db held 0 nodes on 2026-09-27. The plugin also started one server per open session (29 at once, ≈ 1.6 GB), each with its own cache and its own consolidator.

  • Done 2026-09-27: graphonomous@ampersand-plugins disabled in ~/.claude/settings.json and in this

repo's .claude/settings.local.json; the running servers stopped; the database left untouched.

  • What replaces it: the file memory itself — ruled 2026-09-28 (D-078), and there is no Graphonomous v3.

Cross-session memory is Claude Code's file memory for this project (~/.claude/projects/-home-travis-ProjectAmp2/memory/, indexed by MEMORY.md), and it stays the durable store.

  • To search it, use `scripts/memory-search.py "<words>"` (BM25, local, no model). On the 23 real

questions sessions had asked v1, it beat grep and the index.

  • Graphonomous v2 will read the folder and the ruling register as source families. It is a derived

graph over them, never a second store.

  • The proposed v3 (a daemon, a journal, and Jev/Ollaya judging recall and relations) was benchmarked and

closed. Governed Jev asserted 6 false supersedes, at a confidence no threshold could separate from its correct ones.

  • The record is graphonomous/docs/spec/v3/README.md §C; the survivors are in

graphonomous/v2/handoff/ROADMAP.md.

  • Two disciplines survive: never fabricate provenance, outcomes, causal links or coverage signals;

never state confidence the evidence does not carry.

  • History, not instructions: graphonomous/docs/skills/, AmpersandBoxDesign/prompts/DUAL_LOOP_MACHINES.md

and PRISM/docs/DUAL_LOOP_MACHINES.md describe v1's five machines. The Fly app graphonomous-mcp still serves fleetprompt.com and PRISM and is torn down last under R96.

Three-protocol stack: [&] + PULSE + PRISM

OS-010 PULSE is the temporal algebra that lets every loop in the [&] portfolio declare its phases, cadence, nesting, substrates, invariants, and cross-loop signal connections in a single JSON file (<loop>.pulse.json). Together with [&] (structural composition) and PRISM (diagnostic measurement), they form the three-protocol stack:

  • [&] composes capabilities (*.ampersand.json) — structural

  • PULSE declares loops + circulation (*.pulse.json) — temporal — see PULSE/schemas/pulse-loop-manifest.v0.1.json

  • PRISM measures loops over time (BYOR benchmark) — diagnostic

Every portfolio product declares its own loop topology in a "PULSE Loop Manifest" section of <project>/docs/spec/README.md. Reference manifests live in PULSE/manifests/ (graphonomous, prism, agentromatic). PRISM does not require a separate file — it reads any system's PULSE manifest directly to discover phases, signatures, and substrates.

The five canonical PULSE phase kinds — retrieve, route, act, learn, consolidate — match the Graphonomous machine architecture exactly. The six canonical cross-loop tokens (as of PULSE v0.1.1) — TopologyContext, DeliberationResult, OutcomeSignal, ReputationUpdate, ConsolidationEvent, SurpriseSignal — flow through CloudEvents v1 envelopes between loops. SurpriseSignal was added in v0.1.1 for GRASP forward-model-prediction-error emission.

When working in any subdirectory, treat the local PULSE Loop Manifest as authoritative for that project's loop topology. Cross-loop integrations should reference manifest connections, not hard-coded coupling.

Arithmetic ladder / box-and-box (the governance kernel)

box-and-box (at AmpersandBoxDesign/box-and-box/) is the [&] governance kernel — an eight-rung modality ladder, each rung a small algebra with stated laws:

  1. alethic (value) — what can happen · 2. axiological (score) — how to rank · 3. deontic (norm/govern) — what's allowed · 4. temporal (supervise) — safe over time · 5. reflexive — may the rules change (entrenched ring-0 core) · 6. epistemic — do we know enough · 7. strategic — who can ensure it · 8. resource — can we afford it (affine ledger).

One composing bridge (bridge.mjs) runs floor-then-gradient: `feasible ▸ permitted ▸ best` over an un-weakenable safety floor; every verdict ships a certificate. 210 enforced property-tested laws + 3 declared-open (109 kernel + 101 compose/CC2 — 100 suite + 1 anchor; node test/laws.mjs && node test/compose-laws.mjs, 2000 trials each). Both suites now derive their printed totals; do not hand-type a law count anywhere, that is exactly how the published and printed numbers drifted apart before. The 3 open gaps (CP5/CP6/CP7, the Value.pi carrier) print FALSIFIED in red by design and the build fails if one starts passing. Invariant Arithmetic (the prior opensentience.org/invariant-arithmetic.html + the TS port in workbench/app/src/lib/ia/) is rungs 1–2 of this same ladder.

Important — the 8 rungs are orthogonal to PULSE's 5 phase kinds. Do NOT claim a 1:1 mapping. The rungs govern a single decision (a one-shot verdict: may this action proceed, and is it best?); PULSE's retrieve/route/act/learn/consolidate sequence a loop over time. The kernel governs what is allowed to happen at a phase — it is not itself a set of phases. The package is pure library, code only (no bundled HTML); the rung "living-paper" pages + interactive playground.html (109 laws wired client-side — the whole kernel suite; re-measured 2026-08-24 on a fresh origin (port 8931, first load) by pressing the page's own button, which reports 109 laws · 109 passing · 0 failing in 437.9 ms. The served copy under `opensentience.org/box-and-box/` is a MANUAL COPY of `AmpersandBoxDesign/box-and-box/` and nothing syncs it — the 2026-08-24 measure needed resource.mjs, test/laws.mjs and LAW_MANIFEST.json copied across first, and without that the playground would have kept reporting the old count while every other surface said 109. The old "64 of 116" was stale in both halves and the note that replaced it was stale in one: the denominator is the derived 210, not 116 and not 123, and the 64 had gone un-re-counted long enough to be quoted three times. Measure this on a fresh origin. The 2026-08-23 re-measure first read 106 laws · 103 passing · 3 failing, which was the browser serving a cached resource.mjs to a freshly-imported laws.mjs — a cache-busting query on the module you import does not bust the cache of the modules it imports. A second port settled it.) are website content at opensentience.org/ root; conformance is published at ampersandboxdesign.com/laws.html.
